meta.title: My Autumn Book — Set 1
meta.subject: English Reading
meta.description: Story comprehension and key autumn events from 'My Autumn Book'.

questions.question: Where does the spider spin its silken thread in the story?
options: In a corner of the garden shed
On the kitchen table
Under the narrator's bed
On top of the school roof
questions.explanation: The story mentions: 'In a corner of the garden shed, Spider spins a silken thread.'

questions.question: The woodpecker agrees that summer is leaving by making a rap-a-tap drumming sound.
questions.explanation: True. The woodpecker agrees with the cicada and drums to show that autumn is coming.

questions.question: What does the squirrel dig a hole to bury in the ground?
options: Its old winter toys
Its warm winter jacket
Its hidden treasure
Its colorful leaves
questions.explanation: The story says: 'Squirrel digs a hole to bury its treasure' to prepare for the change in weather.

questions.question: The caterpillar knows it is time to build a cocoon.
questions.explanation: True. The caterpillar knows that autumn is coming, so it is time to cocoon.

questions.question: Which birds fly south in formation while honking above?
options: Blue Jays
Geese
Woodpeckers
Robins
questions.explanation: The story says: 'Geese honk above, Fly south in formation.'

questions.question: When a chilly wind blows, the narrator zips up their _______.
questions.hint: A short coat worn to stay warm.
questions.explanation: The text says: 'A chilly wind blows. I zip my jacket.'

questions.question: The oak tree changes into a suit of yellow, while the ash tree changes into crimson.
questions.explanation: False. In the story, the oak changes into rust brown, the ash is in yellow, and the dogwood is in crimson.

questions.question: Sort these actions based on whether the Narrator or the Animals do them in the story:
questions.explanation: The narrator zips their jacket, empties their pack, and decorates pages. Animals like the caterpillar cocoon and the squirrel digs a hole.

questions.question: Arrange the words to show what the narrator does to the pages:
questions.explanation: Correct sentence: 'I decorate my pages.' The narrator makes a book of autumn leaves.

questions.question: Why does the chipmunk scamper past with seeds packed in its cheeks?
options: To find food for the upcoming weeks
To show its cheeks to the woodpecker
To give the seeds to the spider
To hide from the cold rain
questions.explanation: The story says: 'Chipmunk scampers past, Seeds packed in its cheeks, Finding food for the upcoming weeks.'

questions.question: The Blue Jay cries 'Ker-YAK!' because it is surprised that autumn is arriving so soon.
questions.explanation: True. The Blue Jay cries 'Ker-YAK! Autumn so soon?' as a sign of surprise at the changing season.

questions.question: The swirling and twirling leaves make a _______ of color that blankets the ground.
questions.explanation: The story describes the falling leaves as 'A whirlwind of color that blankets the ground.'

questions.question: Arrange the words to describe what the seasons are doing in the story:
questions.explanation: Correct sentence: 'The seasons are changing.' This is why summer leaves and autumn comes.

questions.question: The crickets sing louder and louder late at night when the world turns cold and white.
questions.explanation: False. The book ends by stating: 'When crickets no longer sing late at night and the world outside has turned cold...'

questions.question: What is the main idea of 'My Autumn Book'?
options: How a spider weaves webs to catch bugs
Observing nature and collecting signs of summer leaving and autumn arriving
Learning how to grow pine trees and keep needles green
How to stay warm indoors when winter comes
questions.explanation: The main theme is looking for natural clues that show autumn is on the way and documenting them in a leaf scrapbook.
